description: Charging session view: BMS charge states, charger mains and DC side, cell spread and pack temperature during a charge.

options.content:
Charge telemetry from CAN `0x201` (BMS system state), `0x10A` (charge current limit) and the
charger frames (`mains_v`, `mains_a`, `dc_v`, `dc_a`, `charger_enabled`, `charger_max_dc_*`).

**What is captured so far.** The 2026-08-02 session contains one AC charge: about 48 minutes from
16:55 to 17:43, 224 V and 3.2 A on the mains side, roughly 2.3 A at 295 V on the DC side, SOC 38 to
39 %, +0.9 Ah. Everything on this dashboard that reads off those signals has real data behind it.

**What is still empty, and why.** These have never been seen non-zero, so their panels and lanes
stay blank until a longer or fuller charge is captured. That is the signal being absent, not a
broken query:

- `bms_state_trickle`, `bms_state_balancing`, `bms_state_charge_complete`, `bms_state_maintenance`
  and `bms_state_idle` - the pack only ever reported Discharge or Charge. Balancing runs at the top
  of charge, so `cell_spread_mv` during balancing needs a charge that actually reaches full.
- `charging` (`0x102` bit) - that decoder only started sampling after the charge had ended, so the
  bit is recorded as 0 throughout. `bms_state_charge` off `0x201` is the reliable charge flag and is
  what the annotations use.
- `charge_port_unlocked` - three samples, all parked.
- `go` - the GO signal has only ever been 0 in the capture, so the GO annotation draws nothing
  here either. `ride-summary.json` has a GO lane in its State panel to check that against; this dashboard does not,
  so read the empty annotation as the signal being flat rather than the query failing.

**When the charge-session tiles overstate.** `bms_state_charge` closes a session with a 0, and
the four tiles fall back to the end of the range when there is no closing 0 yet. That is right
for a charge still running and wrong for one the bike slept through before logging the 0: the
session then reads open-ended until the next power-on writes that 0, and the three delta tiles
can go negative once the bike has been ridden since. Clamping to the last row on the bus instead
would be worse - the 2026-08-02 charge has stretches of 26 minutes with no `pack_v` row and 17
minutes with no row of any signal, because a resting pack at 3 A changes nothing worth logging,
so that clamp would under-report every real charge by up to that much. Read a suspiciously long
charging time against the BMS system state lanes below.

**Reading the panels.** Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a flat stretch
means "unchanged", not "missing". Every series uses stepAfter with spanNulls on for that reason.

panels.description: Last charge_state, the raw System State byte out of 0x201 b0. Bit 0 Discharge, bit 1 Charge, bit 2 Balancing, bit 3 Trickle, bit 4 Idle, bit 5 Charge complete, bit 6 Maintenance. The mapping covers the single-bit values; a combination shows as its raw number, and the lanes further down are the reliable way to read overlapping states.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "BMS state"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'charge_state' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: BMS state

panels.description: Length of the most recent charge session, bounded by the bms_state_charge edges rather than by the range itself, so it does not grow when the range also covers a ride. The session is the most recent one that started at or before the end of the range: the last 0 to 1 edge of bms_state_charge, through to the first 0 after it. Both edges are found outside the range if that is where they are, so this reports the whole session whether the range is zoomed into the middle of a charge or panned off its end, and two charges in one range describe the later one instead of being merged with the gap between them counted. A session with no closing 0 yet reads up to the end of the range - see the About panel for when that overstates.

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH charge_flag AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts, r.value AS value, LAG(r.value) OVER (ORDER BY r.ts) AS previous_value
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_charge'
),
last_start AS (
  SELECT MAX(ts) AS started FROM charge_flag
  WHERE value = 1 AND (previous_value IS NULL OR previous_value = 0) AND ts <= $__to
),
session AS (
  SELECT last_start.started AS started,
         COALESCE((SELECT MIN(later.ts) FROM charge_flag later
                   WHERE later.value = 0 AND later.ts > last_start.started), $__to) AS ended
  FROM last_start WHERE last_start.started IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT session.ended/1000.0 AS time, session.ended - session.started AS "Charging time"
FROM session WHERE session.ended >= $__from

panels.title: Charging time

panels.description: Last minus first soc across the charge session. SOC is a 1 % integer, so a short top-up can legitimately read 0. The session is the most recent one that started at or before the end of the range: the last 0 to 1 edge of bms_state_charge, through to the first 0 after it. Both edges are found outside the range if that is where they are, so this reports the whole session whether the range is zoomed into the middle of a charge or panned off its end, and two charges in one range describe the later one instead of being merged with the gap between them counted. A session with no closing 0 yet reads up to the end of the range - see the About panel for when that overstates.

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH charge_flag AS (
  SELECT r.ts AS ts, r.value AS value, LAG(r.value) OVER (ORDER BY r.ts) AS previous_value
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_charge'
),
last_start AS (
  SELECT MAX(ts) AS started FROM charge_flag
  WHERE value = 1 AND (previous_value IS NULL OR previous_value = 0) AND ts <= $__to
),
session AS (
  SELECT last_start.started AS started,
         COALESCE((SELECT MIN(later.ts) FROM charge_flag later
                   WHERE later.value = 0 AND later.ts > last_start.started), $__to) AS ended
  FROM last_start WHERE last_start.started IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT session.ended/1000.0 AS time,
  (SELECT l.value FROM reading l JOIN signal ls ON ls.id = l.signal_id
   WHERE ls.key = 'soc' AND l.ts <= session.ended + 2000
   ORDER BY l.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  - (SELECT f.value FROM reading f JOIN signal fs ON fs.id = f.signal_id
     WHERE fs.key = 'soc' AND f.ts <= session.started + 2000
     ORDER BY f.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  AS "SOC gained"
FROM session WHERE session.ended >= $__from

panels.title: SOC gained

Both edges are found outside the range if that is where they are, so this reports the whole session whether the range is zoomed into the middle of a charge or panned off its end, and two charges in one range describe the later one instead of being merged with the gap between them counted. A session with no closing 0 yet reads up to the end of the range - see the About panel for when that overstates.

panels.title: Energy added

panels.description: Last charger_enabled. Tracks bms_state_charge closely but comes from the charger frame, so it is a useful second opinion on whether the charger itself was commanded on.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Charger enabled"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'charger_enabled' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Charger enabled

panels.description: The seven bms_state_* booleans decoded from the 0x201 System State byte, one lane each. A state timeline suits these far better than lines: each stored row is an edge and the value holds until the next one. In the current capture only Discharge and Charge ever go on; the other five lanes sit at "no" and will stay that way until a charge reaches balancing or completion.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Discharge"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_discharge' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Charge"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_charge' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Trickle"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_trickle' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Balancing"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_balancing' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Charge complete"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_charge_complete' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Idle"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_idle' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Maintenance"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_maintenance' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

panels.title: BMS system state

panels.description: Last mains_v. Fixed V suffix rather than Grafana's volt, which applies SI prefixes.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Mains voltage"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'mains_v' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Mains voltage

panels.description: MAX of mains_a over the range.

targets.rawQueryText:

FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'mains_a' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Peak mains current

panels.description: Last dc_v, the charger's output voltage into the pack. Sits a few volts above pack_v while current is flowing.

targets.rawQueryText:

WHERE s.key = 'dc_v' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: DC voltage

panels.description: MAX of dc_a over the range. Only 7 rows exist in the 2026-08-02 capture, so this is a coarse figure; mains current is the better-sampled one.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, MAX(r.value) AS "Peak DC current"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'dc_a' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Peak DC current

panels.description: Last charge_limit_a from 0x10A b7. This is the limit the bike is asking for, not what is flowing.

targets.rawQueryText:

ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Charge current limit

panels.description: Last charger_max_dc_a, the charger's own ceiling. Reads 0 when the charger is off.

panels.title: Charger max DC current

panels.description: mains_v on the left axis, mains_a on the right. Mains current is only published while the charger is drawing, so the trace stops rather than falling to zero when charging ends. Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Mains voltage"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'mains_v' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Mains current"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'mains_a' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

panels.title: Mains side

panels.description: dc_v on the left axis, dc_a on the right. dc_a is sparse (7 rows in the current capture) because it only changes in 0.1 A steps at a low charge rate. Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

targets.rawQueryText:

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "DC current"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'dc_a' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

panels.title: DC side

panels.description: charge_limit_a (what the bike asks for), charger_max_dc_a (what the charger can do) and dc_a (what actually flowed). All three are step-held between samples. Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Charge limit"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'charge_limit_a' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Charger max DC"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "DC current"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id

panels.title: Current limits vs delivered

panels.description: pack_v on the left axis, soc on the right. pack_v is the densest signal in the database; soc moves in 1 % steps, so its trace is a staircase. Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

targets.rawQueryText:

WHERE s.key = 'soc' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

panels.title: Pack voltage and SOC

panels.description: cell_spread_mv is max minus min computed from 0x203; cell_deviation_mv is the BMS's own max-min out of 0x205, so the two are independent takes on the same thing and should track. This is the panel to watch during a charge: balancing only runs near the top of charge, so a spread that keeps growing as the pack fills is the interesting failure. Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Cell spread (0x203)"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'cell_spread_mv' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Cell deviation (0x205)"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'cell_deviation_mv' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

panels.title: Cell spread

panels.description: batt_temp_hi against the coolant outlet probe. AC charging at 3 A barely warms the pack; the reason to keep the panel is that a fast charge should show up here first. coolant_out is bounded to -20..100 C so a probe dropout cannot distort the axis. Values are logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so a gap means "unchanged", not "missing". stepAfter + spanNulls therefore draws exactly what was recorded; linear interpolation would invent samples that were never on the bus.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Battery (hottest)"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'batt_temp_hi' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS "Coolant out"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'coolant_out' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND r.value BETWEEN -20 AND 100
ORDER BY r.ts

panels.title: Charge temperatures

panels.description: charger_enabled from the charger frame, charging from 0x102 and charge_port_unlocked. The 0x102 charging bit has no coverage during the captured charge - its decoder started afterwards - which is exactly why the annotations key off 0x201 instead.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Charger enabled"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'charger_enabled' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Charging (0x102)"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'charging' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Charge port unlocked"
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
WHERE s.key = 'charge_port_unlocked' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
ORDER BY r.ts

panels.title: Charge flags

title: Cool Eva — Charging
